searchText: Hey all, good morning 🙂 Any stance from the EIP-7702 authors on the EIP-161 situation? 🤔 https://github.com/ethereum/tests/releases/tag/v14.0 Are you interested in contribution some basic EVM tests to EEST? E.g. for `MUL` or stack underflow for each opcode? Yes by all means that would be great 😄 We actually have a `ethereum/tests` -> `eest` porting procedure, where you add the tests that you ported in a PR to a file, and our CI will automatically run a coverage diff as an extra to guarantee that the tests at least have the same or better coverage. That plus a proper review can give us the guarantee that the test files in `ethereum/tests` can be considered legacy. <@393119312350543872> can comment a bit more on this process We tried it for EOF migration and it said "coverage lost". I think we should try with something simpler first because there are no "successful" migrations yet. Definitely, I think a failure on this CI item should not block a PR from merging, but it would be nice to add it to the test porting file just to keep track of this I am trying to get eip1153 pr as an example now for a long time It also generates the html report. Yes the script in test mode, but with state tests its pretty reliable. Also you can trigger coverage re run any moment by touching the .py files and lines in .txt file. <@425274498732916736> in your pr it wasn't able to detect the coverage as filling of .py files failed with errors https://github.com/ethereum/execution-spec-tests/actions/runs/9740081520/job/26876488104?pr=647 Also the tests are filling pre eof fork for some reason as well. The tool ignores fork but pyspec os filling it allover again Is this a complain? This is to answer why there is still not a successful migration yet. That pr was a demo of the script since 2 months or so. The process review change review change is slow indeed especially given the test convertion is not a priority. <@425274498732916736> the latest version of evmone fails to generate test_returncontract.py eof tests the old one is fine so I would not neglect coverage script. we can detect this issues It's only because the test is outdated. And it takes a lot of time to get it updated. ah so it is not ready yet ? why then you say the coverage script didn't work I'm not saying it doesn't work, but the output is unreadable (if it fails it is hard to tell what's wrong). e.g. > docker: Error response from daemon: toomanyrequests: You have reached your pull rate limit. You may increase the limit by authenticating and upgrading: https://www.docker.com/increase-rate-limit. This is new. Docker hub blocked us. <@892053833121923094> perhaps downloading images from ethdevops was a better idea? Yes there are rooms for improvement. Now on real use cases we see
